item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"The title is a metaphorical value judgment presenting service information as functionally important to repair, as requested.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes an unsupported generalization about how the right-to-repair debate is commonly framed.","claims":[{"claim":"The right-to-repair debate is often framed primarily as a dispute over access to parts.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Across representative right-to-repair advocacy, legislation, and industry responses, how frequently is the debate framed as a dispute over parts?"}]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"keep","reason":"The possibility that withheld service information is a shop's first practical obstacle follows from the requested premise, while the parenthetical and list identify kinds of service information without asserting their prevalence.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The request supplies withholding as intellectual property and permits the map metaphor and resulting diagnostic burden, but it does not establish that manufacturers state protection of creative work as their defense.","claims":[{"claim":"Manufacturers that withhold service information as intellectual property state that protecting creative work is a reason for doing so.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which manufacturers have expressly defended withholding service information on the ground that it protects creative work, and in what statements or policies?"}]},{"id":"p2s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical value judgment denying that a manual's role is merely decorative.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is the requested governing metaphor and value judgment about a manual's practical function.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts a proposition about the scope and operation of intellectual-property protection that is not supplied by the request.","claims":[{"claim":"Intellectual-property protections can protect a repair manual's original expression without treating every useful fact about the machine as a protected company secret.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Under the relevant intellectual-property and trade-secret regimes, which parts of repair documentation can be protected as original expression, and which functional facts remain outside that protection?"}]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes unsupported general claims about the content of repair manuals and characterizes listed information as factual descriptions of device operation.","claims":[{"claim":"Repair manuals may contain expressive writing.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do representative repair manuals contain copyrightable expressive writing, and what portions qualify?"},{"claim":"Connector locations, error codes, and test values commonly form the practical core of repair manuals and describe how purchased devices function.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do representative repair manuals use connector locations, error codes, and test values as functional descriptions needed for repair?"}]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"keep","reason":"Given the supplied withholding premise, this is an evaluative contrast: treating all service information as proprietary obstructs the requested maintenance purpose rather than serving the asserted value of creativity.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes causal generalizations about technicians' inability to compensate for missing specifications and about the effects of guesswork.","claims":[{"claim":"A technician cannot reliably replace a missing voltage specification through skill or ingenuity alone.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"In what repair contexts is a specified voltage indispensable rather than independently measurable or inferable by a technician?"},{"claim":"Diagnostic guesswork caused by missing specifications increases repair time and can damage equipment.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that specification-related diagnostic guesswork increases repair time or causes equipment damage?"}]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The request asks for the cost to small shops but does not establish the comparative claim that this cost falls on them more heavily than on other actors.","claims":[{"claim":"The costs caused by withheld service information fall more heavily on small repair shops than on larger repair organizations.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How do the costs of unavailable service information compare between small independent shops and larger repair organizations?"}]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts an unsupported economic advantage enjoyed by large service networks.","claims":[{"claim":"Large service networks can distribute diagnostic-subscription, specialized-equipment, and training expenses across many locations.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do large service networks commonly share or amortize these expenses across locations, and how does that affect per-repair costs?"}]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"disclose","reason":"Although the two-technician example is signaled as hypothetical, the sentence makes an unsupported general comparison about independent shops' repair volume and cost recovery.","claims":[{"claim":"Independent repair operations generally have fewer repairs over which to recover diagnostic-subscription, equipment, and training charges than large service networks do.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How do repair volume and the recovery of diagnostic, equipment, and training costs compare between independent shops and large service networks?"}]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a direct opportunity-cost inference: the same hour devoted to tracing the undocumented circuit cannot simultaneously be used for other paid work.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s5","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes unsupported causal claims about uncertainty, teardown risk, pricing, and customer acceptance.","claims":[{"claim":"Uncertainty about labor and the possibility of a second teardown makes shops less able to offer repairs at prices customers will accept.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How do uncertain labor estimates and possible repeat teardowns affect quoted prices, repair offers, and customer acceptance?"}]},{"id":"p4s6","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts that otherwise viable repair jobs are actually excluded from shop queues.","claims":[{"claim":"Some economically or technically viable repair jobs are not accepted because of the costs or uncertainty created by unavailable service information.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Is there evidence that independent shops decline otherwise viable jobs because required service information is unavailable?"}]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The requested link between documentation and parts pairing does not by itself establish the categorical causal claim that documentation determines whether a replacement part is usable.","claims":[{"claim":"Access to documentation determines whether replacement parts are usable in at least some repairs.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"For which devices or repairs does access to documentation determine whether a replacement part can be successfully used?"}]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"keep","reason":"This supplies a definition of the requested concept of parts pairing; the parenthetical gives illustrative forms of software authorization rather than reporting their prevalence.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts real technical behaviors that paired devices may exhibit after installation of a physically compatible part.","claims":[{"claim":"Some devices reject physically compatible replacement parts, limit their functions, or display persistent warnings because of parts-pairing controls.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which devices exhibit rejection, functional limits, or persistent warnings after installation of physically compatible replacement parts, and under what conditions?"}]},{"id":"p5s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative conception of meaningful ownership and a demand that installation information and procedures accompany replacement hardware.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is an inference from the requested link between documentation and parts pairing: withholding the documentation can strengthen the pairing barrier.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a conditional inference from the definition of pairing: if only the manufacturer supplies the withheld authorization procedure, replacement depends on manufacturer participation.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s3","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence states a qualified logical consequence of withholding diagnostic documentation: without differentiating information, the shop may be unable to distinguish among the listed possible fault categories.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s4","status":"keep","reason":"The card-catalog and library language is a coherent analogy for the supplied premise that information is needed to make practical use of repair parts.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a recommendation defining desirable qualities of the proposed disclosure rule.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s2","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence proposes who must disclose what, to whom, and on what terms; it makes no claim about current practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a proposed limitation on the disclosure rule rather than a description of existing legal requirements.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s4","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence proposes the rule's scope and supports it with a metaphorical judgment that access to physical tools alone does not remove an information or authentication barrier.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a recommendation that the proposed rule include a simple evaluative test.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a clearly signaled hypothetical question illustrating the proposed test, not a report of an actual sensor installation.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s3","status":"keep","reason":"This defines conditions under which the proposed rule should deem disclosure inadequate; the examples are components of that normative definition.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative balancing principle allowing tailored safeguards while rejecting security as an unlimited justification for withholding routine procedures.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is a recommendation that safeguards be risk-specific and preserve lawful repair.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is an expressly normative demand for lawmakers to treat repair information as infrastructure of ownership.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s2","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence recommends enforcement, update coverage, and a prohibition on locks that defeat disclosed instructions.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s3","status":"keep","reason":"This recommends implementation guidance and a complaint process for agencies that would administer the proposed rule.","claims":[]},{"id":"p10s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence predicts the real-world competitive effect of disclosure and presupposes existing manufacturer or large-chain advantages.","claims":[{"claim":"Manufacturers and large service chains hold advantages over independent repair shops that a service-information disclosure rule would not eliminate.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What advantages do manufacturers and large service chains currently hold, and which of them would remain after the proposed disclosures?"}]},{"id":"p10s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The fairness language is evaluative, but the sentence also predicts that disclosure will improve independent shops' ability to compete and characterizes current competition as affected by privileged access.","claims":[{"claim":"Providing the proposed disclosures would improve independent shops' ability to compete on skill, price, and service.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence indicates that access to service information, pairing procedures, software, and calibration tools improves independent shops' competitive ability?"},{"claim":"Manufacturers or authorized service organizations possess privileged access to repair information or tools unavailable to independent shops.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What repair information or tools are available to manufacturers or authorized service organizations but unavailable to independent shops?"}]},{"id":"p10s3","status":"keep","reason":"This states a proposed public-interest principle and legal requirement triggered by a company's sale of a repairable product.","claims":[]},{"id":"p10s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a call to action urging readers to advocate for the proposed rule.","claims":[]}]}
